verdicts.line: You roar. Everyone who witnesses it is frightened, whatever you intend.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the roar frightens all who witness it, whatever you intend
verdicts.reason: Direct lift from the tutorial narration description, preserving the crucial 'whatever you intend' paradox that makes this uhta-specific.

verdicts.line: Roar. The earth shatters ahead — and everyone who sees you do it becomes afraid.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: you roar and the earth shatters ahead
verdicts.reason: Combines the tutorial's exact phrasing with the witness-fear mechanic, maintaining both the verb name and its dual consequence.

verdicts.line: You roar and the ground breaks open. All who witness it feel fear, no matter what your flame holds.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: no matter what your flame holds
verdicts.reason: Captures the unconditional Fear push mechanic and the flame-independence that defines Roar's unique position in the verb set.

verdicts.line: Roar: it clears the path fast, but everyone who watches is pushed toward fear — even when you carry hope.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: Shatters a line of tiles — fast traversal / path creation
verdicts.reason: Names both consequences (terrain work and emotional push) and explicitly states the flame-color exception that makes this verb mechanically distinct.

verdicts.line: You can roar to shatter the earth. Everyone within sight of the breaking will be frightened, regardless of what you feel.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: NPCs within witness radius R (~6 tiles) of the line take an unconditional Fear push
verdicts.reason: Uses 'within sight' instead of the witness-radius concept, and 'will be frightened' softens the unconditional mechanical push to generic emotional language.
verdicts.correction: You can roar to shatter the earth. Everyone within witness radius takes fear — unconditional, regardless of what you feel.

verdicts.line: Roar shatters a line of ground ahead of you. Anyone who witnesses the act is made afraid — your flame's color doesn't matter.
verdicts.reason: Preserves the line-geometry of the verb and the flame-independence clause that distinguishes Roar from Raise mechanically.

verdicts.line: You roar and the land splits. Every witness is frightened by what they see, whatever emotion you carry.
verdicts.reason: 'Frightened by what they see' implies reaction to spectacle rather than the mechanical push; 'whatever emotion you carry' is weaker than the flame-color independence.
verdicts.correction: You roar and the land splits. Every witness takes fear — unconditional, whatever your flame's color.

verdicts.line: Roar breaks the earth in a line. All who see it happen are afraid — the flame you hold changes nothing.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the flame you hold changes nothing
verdicts.reason: Strongest statement of the flame-independence mechanic, making explicit what distinguishes Roar from every other verb in the system.
